(Also known as: norflurazone; H 9789; monometflurazon)
SUMMARY
Hazard alerts

The following Pesticide Hazard Tricolour (PHT) alerts are based on the data in the tables below. An absence of an alert does not imply the substance has no implications for human health, biodiversity or the environment but just that we do not have the data to form a judgement. The alerts for Highly Hazardous Pesticides (HHPs) are based on applying the FAO/WHO (Type 1) and the PAN (Type II) criteria to PPDB data. Further details on the HHP indicators are given in the tables below. Neither the PHT nor the HHP hazard alerts take account of usage patterns or exposure, thus they do not represent risk.

Formulation and application details
Available in a variety of formulations including wettable powders, flowable concentrates and granules
Commercial production
The industrial synthesis of norflurazon begins with the formation of the pyridazinone ring, typically derived from hydrazine and diketone precursors. This heterocyclic core is then functionalized by introducing a trifluoromethyl-substituted aromatic group via nucleophilic substitution or coupling reactions. The methylamino and chloro substituents are introduced through selective halogenation and amination steps, often using reagents like methylamine and phosphorus oxychloride. These reactions are carried out in organic solvents such as acetonitrile or dimethylformamide, under controlled temperature and pH conditions to ensure high yield and regioselectivity.
